title: Fixing bugs in Gemma, Llama, & Phi 3: Daniel Han
talk_summary: Daniel Han walks through concrete bugs found in Gemma, Llama 3, and Phi 3 model configs and fine-tuning setups (double BOS tokens, untrained special tokens causing NaN gradients, pad==EOS causing infinite generation, chat-template mismatches) and how Unsloth auto-detects and fixes them. The talk is almost entirely about LLM fine-tuning internals, not agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Automated pre-flight config validation with known-bug checks
takeaways.what_they_do: Unsloth runs automatic checks before training (double BOS, pad==EOS, untrained tokens) and silently fixes them, rather than relying on the user to notice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in unsoft we do this we check this automatically and we'll remove the extra BOS token automatically for you

takeaways.technique: Encode known-defect signatures as explicit checks
takeaways.what_they_do: They catalogued specific, named bug classes (double BOS, pad==EOS, untrained tokens) and turned each into a checkable rule with a fix, instead of generic 'review the model'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's actually eight bugs in llama 3 ... we'll be going through each of them separately

takeaways.technique: Warn on known-bad patterns at the tool boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: llama.cpp added a runtime warning when double-BOS is detected, so the failure surfaces at the point of use rather than after a broken fine-tune.
takeaways.evidence_quote: llama CPP now has a warning for you to tell you that you're using wbos tokens

takeaways.technique: Offload to RAM before disk; non-blocking calls
takeaways.what_they_do: For long-context training they offload gradient checkpoints to system RAM (non-blocking) rather than disk, and warn that disk offload or blocking calls make runs extremely slow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: please do not do that if you offload to dis then your your time of completion of your fine tune will be extremely slow

takeaways.technique: Match configured context length to actual data size
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that setting max sequence length far above the dataset size wastes memory and prevents effective long-context training; the setting must match the data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your data set must match the max sequence length ... try to like not set that Max sequence left to be that large
